Rashi on Pesachim 22b:10:1.english: And the other - [The one] who derives [the prohibition against] benefit from the hide from [the word] "clear":

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:10:2.hebrew: את לא דריש - לריבויא, דסבר לה כשמעון העמסוני, שפירש כל אתים שבתורה לרבות. כיון שהגיע ל"את ה' אלהיך תירא", אמר: "מה ארבה לירא עמו?!" פירש מכולן, וחזר בו מכל ריבויין שדרש — דמדהא לאו לרבוייא אתא, כולהו נמי לאו לרבויי אתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:10:2.english: Does not interpret et - As an amplification; for he holds in accordance with Shimon HaAmsoni, who explained all [instances of] et in the Torah [as coming] to include. Once he reached “You shall fear the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 10:20), he said: “What can I include to be feared along with Him?!” He withdrew from all of them and retracted all the amplifications he had expounded — for since this [instance] did not come for amplification, all of them likewise did not come for amplification.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:11:1.english: To include Torah scholars - That the fear of your teacher should be like the fear of Heaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:12:1.hebrew: ולא יצבע בו - כגון בקליפי אגוזים, שהשומר אסור משום ערלה כפרי עצמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:12:1.english: Nor may he dye with it - For example, with walnut shells, as the protective covering is forbidden due to [the prohibition of] orlah like the fruit itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:12:2.english: Nor may he light a lamp with it - For example, with oil of orlah.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:15:1.english: And now that these verses are written - To prohibit it [from benefit].

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:15:2.english: To you - Which implies permission — for what did it come?

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:1:1.hebrew: ולחזקיה - דאמר לעיל: איסור הנאה דחמץ מלא יאכל, הא לא תאכל ולא תאכלו — לא משמע ליה הנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:1:1.english: And according to Ḥizkiya - For he said above [that] the prohibition of benefit from chametz [is derived] from “it shall not be eaten,” whereas “you shall not eat” and “you [plural] shall not eat” do not imply [a prohibition of] benefit to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:1:2.hebrew: למאי הלכתא איתקש דם למים - למשרייה בהנאה, ומהיכא תיתי לך דניתסרו? ומנבילה לא אותביניה לחזקיה: למאי איצטריך קרא למשרייה? דאי כר' יהודה סבר — לדברים ככתבן הוא דאתא, ואי כר"מ סבר — לה איצטריך להקדים נתינה דגר למכירה דנכרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:1:2.english: For what halakha is blood juxtaposed to water - [According to Rabbi Abbahu, it was juxtaposed] to permit it for benefit; and [according to Ḥizkiya,] from where would you derive that it should be forbidden? And from [the verse regarding] an animal carcass (neveila) we did not challenge Ḥizkiya: 'Why was the verse needed to permit it?' — for if he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, it came [to teach that] matters are as they are written; and if he holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, it was needed for this: to give precedence to giving [it] to a resident alien over selling [it] to a gentile.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:2:1.english: You shall not eat the life with the flesh - While the life is [still] in it.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:2:2.hebrew: בני נח - נאסר להם אבר מן החי, דכתיב (בראשית ט׳:ד׳) אך בשר בנפשו דמו לא תאכלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:2:2.english: Descendants of Noah - A limb from a living [animal] is forbidden to them, as it is written: “However, flesh with its life, [which is] its blood, you shall not eat” (Genesis 9:4).

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:2:3.hebrew: לפני עור - אלמא לא מיתסר אלא משום ״לפני עור לא תתן מכשול״, אבל בהנאה אחריתי — כגון לכלב — שרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:2:3.english: Before the blind - Evidently, it is forbidden only on account of “You shall not put a stumbling block before the blind,” but for another benefit — such as [giving it] to a dog — it is permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:3:1.hebrew: לבלתי אכול הדם - סיפיה דקרא: לא תאכל הנפש וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:3:1.english: In not eating the blood - The end of the verse [states]: “You shall not eat the life, etc.”

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:4:1.hebrew: מה אבר מן החי אסור - באיסור האמור בו, אף דם מן החי אסו' באיסו' האמור בו — כלומר כרת, משום דם גמור. מהו דתימא: "רק חזק לבלתי אכול הדם" — אוזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך דכתיב לעיל קאי, ודם זביחה הוא דאסור, אבל דם הקזה מותר:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:4:1.english: Just as a limb from a living [animal] is forbidden - With the prohibition stated regarding it; so too, blood from a living [animal] is forbidden with the prohibition stated regarding it — that is to say, [with] karet, on account of [it being] full-fledged blood. Lest you say [that the verse,] "Only be steadfast not to eat the blood," refers to "and you shall slaughter of your herd and of your flock," which is written above, and [thus] it is [only] blood of slaughter that is forbidden, but blood of bloodletting is permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:4:2.hebrew: ואיזה זה - כלומר: על איזה דם מן החי אסור משום דם, הא דם הנפש כתיב? על דם הקזה של בהמה שהנפש יוצא בו. יש ד' מיני דמים בהיקז, כדאמרינן בכריתות (דף כב.): בתחלה שותת, ולבסוף מקלח, ואחר כך משחיר, וסופו שותת. יש מהן שאין הנשמה יוצאה בו, ויש מהן שהנשמה יוצאה בו. והתם תניא: איזהו דם היקז שהנשמה יוצאה בו? כל זמן שמקלח כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:4:2.english: And which is this - That is to say: Concerning which blood from a living [animal] is [one] prohibited under [the prohibition of] blood, seeing that "the lifeblood" is written [in the Torah]? [It refers] to blood of bloodletting of an animal through which the soul departs. There are four types of blood in bloodletting, as we say in Keritot (22a): At first it trickles, and then it spurts, and afterwards it darkens, and in the end it trickles. There are some among them through which the soul does not depart, and there are some among them through which the soul departs. And there it is taught: "Which is the blood of bloodletting through which the soul departs? As long as it spurts," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:5:1.hebrew: שאם שחטו כו' - והכי אמר קרא: סקול יסקל השור, ואי לא סקלו — אעפ"כ לא יאכל את בשרו:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:5:1.english: That if one slaughtered it, etc. - And this is what the verse is saying: “The ox shall surely be stoned”; and if he did not stone it, nevertheless “its flesh shall not be eaten.”

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:7:1.hebrew: איסור הנאה לא משמע - וקשיא אפילו לחזקיה, וכ"ש לרבי אבהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:7:1.english: The prohibition of benefit is not implied - And [this is] difficult even according to Ḥizkiya, and all the more so according to Rabbi Abbahu.

Rashi on Pesachim 22b:9:1.hebrew: ולהנך תנאי - דבב"ק פ' שור שנגח (בבא קמא דף מא: ומב.), דמפקי ליה להאי נקי לדרשא אחרינא, לאשמעינן דתם פטור מחצי כופר — דקאמר: נקי מחצי כופר אם המית איש, דאילו מועד משלם כופר שלם, והתם אפילו חצי כופר לא משלם. ואיכא דמפיק ליה לדמי וולדות, אם נגח אשה הרה ויצאו ילדיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 22b:9:1.english: And according to those tanna’im - [Namely, those] in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Shor Shenagach (Bava Kamma 41b and 42a), who expound this [word] “clear” for another interpretation, to teach us that an innocuous [ox] is exempt from half-indemnity — for it says [he is] “clear” of half-indemnity if it killed a person, for whereas a forewarned [ox] pays full indemnity, an innocuous [ox] does not pay even half-indemnity. And there is [a tanna] who expounds it for payment for offspring, if it gored a pregnant woman and her offspring departed.

Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:12:1.hebrew: מנין שלא יצבע - וא"ת: כיון דנפקא לן דאסור בהנאה, אמאי איצטריך לאסור צביעה והדלקה? ואור"י: דס"ד דצביעה לא חשיב הנאה, דלא הוי אלא חזותא בעלמא, כדאמר בהגוזל (שם קא. ושם) אהך מילתא גופא. וכן הדלקה, סלקא דעתך דשריא, כיון דהוי דרך ביעורו. ולמ"ד אין שבח עצים בפת, דשרי עצים בהדלקה — הא דאסר קרא הכא, היינו בשמן, דהוי בעין כשדולק בנר; אבל עצים נעשה גחלים, והשלהבת בא מן הגחלים. ואם תאמר: אמאי איצטריך קרא גבי תרומה טמאה להתיר, דדרשי' "לך" — שלך תהא להסיקה תחת תבשילך, דהכא איצטריך קרא למיסר? ויש לומר: דסלקא דעתך דנילף ממעשר הקל, דאסר ביה הבער', דכתיב "לא בערתי ממנו", כדאמר בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת כה. ושם): ומה מעשר הקל אמרה תורה וכו':
Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:12:1.english: From where [do we derive] that one may not dye - And if you say: Since we derive that it is prohibited to derive benefit [from orla], why was it necessary to prohibit dyeing and kindling? And the Ri says that it might enter your mind [to say] that dyeing is not considered a benefit, as it is merely an appearance [chazuta be'alma], as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 101a and there) regarding this exact matter. And similarly, regarding kindling, it might enter your mind [to say] that it is permitted, since it is the manner of its destruction. And according to the one who says [that there is] no enhancement of wood in bread, such that wood is permitted for kindling, that which the verse prohibits here is regarding oil, which is [present] in its tangible state when burning in a lamp; but wood becomes coals, and the flame comes from the coals. And if you say: Why was a verse necessary regarding ritually impure terumah to permit [kindling it], as we expound: "[It shall be] to you" (Numbers 18:8) — it shall be yours to kindle it under your cooked food, seeing that here a verse was necessary to prohibit [it]? And one can say that it might enter your mind [to say] that we should derive [it] from the lenient tithe, regarding which burning is prohibited, as it is written: "I have not removed [bi'arti] any of it" (Deuteronomy 26:14), as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 25a and there): "And if regarding the lenient tithe, the Torah said..." etc.

Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:15:1.hebrew: לכם למ"ל לכדתניא - הקשה הר"י מקורבל: אמאי איצטריך ג' ערלים? ליכתוב תרי ערלים לצביעה והדלקה, ועל כרחך אתי' לכם לנטוע לרבים; דאי להיתר הדלקה אתא — לא לכתוב לכם ולא חד מהנך ערלים, ונאסור מלא יאכל הנאה, ומחד ערלים צביעה, ולהדלקה אין קרא לאסור. ואין לומר: דמלא יאכל משמע לאסור אפילו צביעה והדלקה, ואי הוה כתיב לא יאכל וחד ערלים הוה אסרינן מלא יאכל כל הנאה, וערלים לשום דרשה, והא דמצרכי' קראי לצביעה והדלקה היינו משום דכתב לכם, דלכם משמע להתיר כל הנאה, ולהכי אי הוה כתיב תרי ערלים ולכם הוה שרינן הדלקה — אי אפשר לומר כן, דמלא יאכל לא שמעינן צביעה, דהא חזותא בעלמ' הוא, כדאמר בהגוזל (ב"ק קא. ושם):
Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:15:1.english: "To you," why do I [need this]? As it was taught - R. Isaac of Corbeil asked: Why was it necessary [to have] three [mentions of] arelim? Let [the Torah] write two [mentions of] arelim for dyeing and kindling, and perforce "to you" would come [to include that which is] planted for the public. For if [you were to say that "to you"] came to permit kindling, let [the Torah] write neither "to you" nor one of these [mentions of] arelim, and we would prohibit [general] benefit from "it shall not be eaten," and dyeing from one [mention of] arelim, and for kindling there would be no verse to prohibit [it, leaving it permitted]! And one cannot say that "it shall not be eaten" implies prohibiting even dyeing and kindling, so that had it written "it shall not be eaten" and one [mention of] arelim, we would prohibit all [forms of] benefit from "it shall not be eaten," and [apply] arelim to some [other] exposition, and that which we require verses for dyeing and kindling is only because it wrote "to you," since "to you" implies permitting all benefit, and therefore had it written two [mentions of] arelim and "to you" we would have permitted kindling — it is impossible to say so, for from "it shall not be eaten" we do not derive [a prohibition against] dyeing, since it is merely an appearance, as [the Gemara] says in [chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 101a and there).

Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:2:1.hebrew: ואבר מן החי לבני נח - תימה: כיון דבאבר מן החי של נכרי מיירי, כדאמר בפ"ק דמסכת ע"ג (דף ו: ושם) מדקתני "לא יושיט" ולא קתני "לא יתן", א"כ היכי דייק דשרי בהנאה אי לאו לפני עור? וי"ל: דכיון דבשכר היה אסור להושיט, דאסור להשתכר באיסורי הנאה — אף על גב דדיעבד שכרו מותר, כדמשמע בפ' בתרא דמס' ע"ז (ד' סב.), מכל מקום אסור לכתחלה — ובחנם נמי אסור, דמה שמחזיק לו העכו"ם טובה חשיב כמשתכר. והא דאמר בסוף אלו מציאו' (ב"מ לב:) גבי "אם היתה טעונה יין נסך אין זקוק לה", "ואי אמרת צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא אמאי אין זקוק לה?" — אע"ג דחשיב כמשתכר באיסורי הנאה ואסור אפילו בחנם, מ"מ כיון דאינו מתכוון שיחזיק לו טובה ומשום צער בעל חיים, חשיב כמו לא אפשר ולא מיכוון דשרי. א"נ: "אין זקוק לה" משמע ליה אפילו שלא בפני נכרי, דאין מחזיק לו טובה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:2:1.english: "And a limb from a living animal to descendants of Noah" - [This is] puzzling: Since it is dealing with a limb from a living animal belonging to a gentile, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (6b and there), from [the fact] that it teaches "one may not pass" and does not teach "one may not give" — if so, how does [the Gemara here] infer that it is permitted to benefit [from a limb from a living animal] were it not for "before the blind"? And it can be answered: Since it would be forbidden to pass [it] for a fee, as it is forbidden to earn a profit from items from which benefit is prohibited — even though after the fact his fee is permitted, as is indicated in the last chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (62a), nevertheless it is forbidden ab initio — and [to pass it] for free is also forbidden, because [the fact] that the gentile feels grateful to him is considered like earning a profit. And as for that which [the Gemara] says at the end of [the chapter entitled] Elu Metziot (Bava Metzia 32b) regarding: "If [an animal] was laden with libation wine, he is not bound to attend to it," and "if you say that [preventing] suffering to animals is [a biblical commandment] from the Torah, why is he not bound to attend to it?" — even though [receiving gratitude] is considered like earning a profit from items from which benefit is prohibited and is forbidden even for free, nevertheless, since he does not intend for [the gentile] to feel grateful to him, but [acts solely] because of the suffering of the animal, it is considered like [a case where] "it is impossible [to avoid] and he does not intend [to benefit]," which is permitted. Alternatively, "he is not bound to attend to it" was understood by [the Gemara] to mean even not in the presence of the gentile, where [the gentile] does not feel grateful to him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:8:1.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא בשרו אין עורו לא - וא"ת: לישתוק מעורו ומבשרו! ויש לומר: דאיצטריך בשרו, אע"ג דעבדיה כעין בשר. ומאן דלית ליה הא דרשה — בפ' שור שנגח ד' וה' (ב"ק מא.) אתא לדרשה אחרינא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 22b:8:1.english: It could enter your mind to say: Its flesh, yes; its hide, no - And if you say: Let [the Torah] be silent concerning its hide and its flesh! One can say that [mentioning] “its flesh” was necessary [to teach that] even though he rendered it like [kosher] meat [by slaughtering it, it is forbidden]. And according to the one who does not accept this exposition — in the chapter [entitled] Shor Shenagach Arba’ah VaChamishah (Bava Kamma 41a), [the verse] comes for another exposition.
